set.body:
Goal
Remove the remaining exhaustive-candidate runtime bottleneck without changing the frozen R reference estimand.

Work
Profile the post-GW-14 engine; introduce prepared immutable path measures, cached spatial/edge terms, buffer reuse, batch candidate scheduling, adjacent-coverage warm starts, and an optional compiled kernel where profiling justifies it. Keep the pure-R implementation as the readable oracle and retain automatic numerical fallback.

Acceptance criteria
- Differential tests cover random, sparse, extreme-scale, short-path, and real-path fixtures.
- Fast and reference energies agree within 1e-8; coupling mass, barycentric match, warp, and candidate rank meet frozen tolerances.
- Candidate evaluation order and batch size do not affect scores.
- No unsafe cross-candidate warm start is the sole initialization; every candidate receives a common initialization policy.
- Median 15 x 15 pair time improves at least 4x from the approximately 60 ms GW-14 baseline, with a stretch goal of 10x.
- A representative full fold improves at least 2x beyond GW-14, with a stretch goal of 3x, while peak memory remains bounded and all alignments converge.
- The native backend is optional and falls back cleanly on unsupported platforms; dependency, CRAN, and sanitizer implications are recorded.
set.title: GW-18.5 Build an estimator-preserving batched native Transport backend
